supplements.title: Archimedes: The Method of Mechanical Theorems
supplements.description: Study guide for the Method — Archimedes's mechanical heuristic of weighing geometric slices on an imaginary lever to discover areas and volumes. A pre-trigonometric seed of integral calculus and a rare glimpse of a classical mathematician showing his working rather than his finished proof

supplements.title: Buoyancy and Displacement Lab
supplements.description: Hands-on experiments with buoyancy and volumetric displacement — the crown problem, floating bodies, and the construction of a unit of mass from displacement

supplements.title: Levers and Center of Gravity Lab
supplements.description: Experiments with levers, balance points, and mechanical advantage — Archimedes' law of the lever

supplements.title: Measuring the Earth
supplements.description: Estimating the Earth's circumference à la Eratosthenes — turning a shadow, a known distance, and a single geometric argument into the size of the planet

supplements.title: Measuring with Parallax
supplements.description: The apparent shift of a near object against a far background, turned into a measurement of distance — two viewpoints and a long thin triangle, with the lunar case in Ptolemy

supplements.title: Observing the Celestial Sphere
supplements.description: Identifying the zodiac and ecliptic in Stellarium, watching a planet go retrograde, and computing the Sun's position in Ptolemy's own sexagesimal mean-motion arithmetic — then checking the prediction against the sky

supplements.title: Quadrature of the Parabola Exercises
supplements.description: Working through Archimedes's proof that the area of a parabolic segment is 4/3 the inscribed triangle — a classical finished proof by exhaustion, with exercises that rebuild the argument step by step

supplements.title: Reading Greek Mathematics
supplements.description: Orientation to the structure of Greek mathematical propositions, with notation guidance for Euclid and conceptual primers for Apollonius and Ptolemy

supplements.title: Archimedes: On the Sphere and Cylinder
supplements.description: Study guide for Archimedes's derivation of sphere and cylinder surface areas and volumes — the result he asked to have inscribed on his tomb, and a bridge between Euclidean geometry and later analytic methods

supplements.title: Nicomachus Notation Guide
supplements.description: Nicomachus's verbal descriptions of figurate numbers, perfect numbers, and arithmetic relationships translated to modern notation

supplements.title: Pneumatics and Hydraulics Lab
supplements.description: Simple pneumatic and hydraulic demonstrations inspired by Hero's devices — siphons, pressure, and steam

supplements.title: The Cattle Problem
supplements.description: Archimedes's epigram problem about the Sun's cattle — an indeterminate system of equations that foreshadows Diophantine analysis. A capstone bonus after working through Diophantus

supplements.title: Al-Khwarizmi Exercise Set
supplements.description: Solve Al-Khwarizmi's problems using his rhetorical methods, then again in modern notation — feel the transition from geometric to algebraic reasoning

supplements.title: Al-Khwarizmi Notation Guide
supplements.description: Rhetorical algebra translated to modern symbolic notation — 'a square and ten roots equal thirty-nine' becomes x² + 10x = 39

supplements.title: Alhazen Optics Exercises
supplements.description: Ray diagrams and geometric problems in reflection and refraction using Alhazen's approach

supplements.title: Camera Obscura Lab
supplements.description: Build a camera obscura and experiment with image formation, light propagation, and the behavior of pinhole images

supplements.title: Fibonacci Numeral Exercises
supplements.description: Arithmetic in Roman vs. Hindu-Arabic numerals — long division, multiplication, and the Fibonacci sequence as a study in recurrence

supplements.title: Boyle's Law Lab
supplements.description: Investigating the pressure-volume relationship in gases — reproducing Boyle's key observation with simple apparatus

supplements.title: Counterpoint Exercises
supplements.description: Writing counterpoint in the five species following Fux's method — cantus firmus exercises progressing through each species

supplements.title: Descartes La Géométrie Notation Guide
supplements.description: Descartes' notation and methods in La Géométrie mapped to modern analytic geometry, focused on Livre Premier — a bridge until an original English translation is produced

supplements.title: Galileo Notation Guide
supplements.description: Galileo's proportional reasoning translated to modern equations of motion — ratios become s = ½at²

supplements.title: Huygens Optics Exercises
supplements.description: Applying Huygens' principle to derive the laws of reflection and refraction geometrically

supplements.title: Inclined Plane Lab
supplements.description: Measuring acceleration and testing the times-squared law with an inclined plane — reproducing Galileo's foundational kinematics experiments

supplements.title: Kepler's Three Laws
supplements.description: The key arguments of Astronomia Nova for readers without Latin, the three laws of planetary motion, and exercises verifying the third law with solar system data

supplements.title: Magnetism Lab
supplements.description: Mapping magnetic fields, observing compass needle deflection, and reproducing Gilbert's key experiments with lodestones and iron

supplements.title: Microscopy Lab
supplements.description: Simple microscope observations following Hooke — examining everyday materials at magnification, drawing what you see, and understanding the discovery of cells

supplements.title: Napier Logarithm Exercises
supplements.description: Computing with Napier's original log tables and understanding logarithms as he conceived them

supplements.title: Napier Notation Guide
supplements.description: Napier's original logarithmic definitions and tables translated to modern logarithmic notation

supplements.title: Pascal & Huygens Probability Exercises
supplements.description: Properties of Pascal's triangle, problems from the Pascal-Fermat correspondence, and probability using Huygens' expectation framework

supplements.title: Pendulum Lab
supplements.description: Investigating pendulum motion — period vs. length, amplitude independence, and an introduction to periodic motion

supplements.title: Port-Royal Logic Exercises
supplements.description: Logic problems in the Port-Royal style — propositions, syllogisms, and fallacies, continuing the formal logic thread from Aristotle

supplements.title: Bayes Exercises
supplements.description: Applying Bayesian reasoning to concrete problems — prior and posterior probabilities, updating beliefs with evidence

supplements.title: Bernoulli's Ars Conjectandi
supplements.description: Key results from Ars Conjectandi for non-French readers — combinatorial probability, the law of large numbers, and Bernoulli's contribution to the probability thread

supplements.title: Binary Arithmetic Exercises
supplements.description: Binary conversion, arithmetic operations in base 2, and the conceptual bridge from Leibniz to Shannon and modern computation

supplements.title: Chemistry Lab — Combustion and Gases
supplements.description: Safe, at-home experiments demonstrating conservation of mass in combustion and basic properties of gases — designed around household materials, no hazardous chemicals

supplements.title: Dalton Atomic Theory Exercises
supplements.description: Stoichiometry, atomic weight calculations, and the law of multiple proportions — working with Dalton's atomic theory

supplements.title: Dalton Notation Guide
supplements.description: Dalton's atomic symbols and diagrams translated to modern chemical notation and the periodic table

supplements.title: Lavoisier Notation Guide
supplements.description: Lavoisier's chemical nomenclature translated to modern chemical symbols and formulas

supplements.title: Newton Principia Notation Guide
supplements.description: Newton's geometric calculus translated to modern Leibnizian notation — fluxions and fluents become derivatives and integrals

supplements.title: Opticks Lab
supplements.description: Prism experiments with light dispersion, observing Newton's rings, and exploring the behavior of white light — reproducing Newton's key optical discoveries with safe, household materials

supplements.title: Reading Leviathan
supplements.description: Recommended selections from Leviathan — the key chapters on the state of nature, social contract, and sovereignty, for extracting Hobbes's core arguments from a large text

supplements.title: Reading The Federalist Papers
supplements.description: Recommended key papers from the 85 Federalist essays — Nos. 10, 51, 70, 78, and others essential to understanding the American constitutional design

supplements.title: Reading the Principia
supplements.description: The structure of the Principia — method of first and last ratios, how to work through propositions, and the relationship between Newton's geometric arguments and modern calculus

supplements.title: Reading The Wealth of Nations
supplements.description: Recommended selections from The Wealth of Nations — key chapters on division of labor, markets, and the role of government

supplements.title: Boolean Algebra Exercises
supplements.description: Truth tables, logical operations, and Boolean algebra — building the bridge from Boole's Laws of Thought to digital logic and Shannon's circuits

supplements.title: Carnot: Thermodynamics — Notation Guide & Exercises
supplements.description: Carnot's heat engine analysis translated to modern thermodynamic notation, with exercises on the Carnot cycle, efficiency, and the second law

supplements.title: Cayley: Matrices — Notation Guide & Exercises
supplements.description: Matrix notation, operations, and determinants — introducing linear algebra and building toward its applications in quantum mechanics

supplements.title: Continuity and Infinity
supplements.description: Retracing the continuity thread from Euclid Book X (incommensurable magnitudes) and Archimedes through Dedekind's cuts and Cantor's transfinite numbers — what these formalizations resolve and what new questions they open

supplements.title: DIY Galvanometer Lab
supplements.description: Build a simple galvanometer with copper wire, a battery, and a compass — detecting electric current and understanding the relationship between electricity and magnetism

supplements.title: Electromagnetic Induction Lab
supplements.description: Building a simple motor or generator — demonstrating electromagnetic induction with magnets and coils of wire

supplements.title: Electrostatics Lab
supplements.description: Static electricity experiments with household materials — charging by friction, electrostatic attraction and repulsion, building a simple capacitor

supplements.title: Faraday Exercises
supplements.description: Field line reasoning, electromagnetic induction problems, and Faraday's conceptual approach to electromagnetism

supplements.title: Galton Statistical Methods Notation Guide
supplements.description: Galton's statistical methods translated to modern notation — regression, the normal distribution, and the origins of biometrics

supplements.title: Maxwell Notation Guide
supplements.description: Maxwell's original formulation of electromagnetism mapped to the modern four equations — from 20 equations in component form to the compact vector calculus notation

supplements.title: Mendel Genetics Exercises
supplements.description: Punnett squares, probability of trait inheritance, dominance and recessiveness — connecting Mendel's experiments to the probability thread

supplements.title: Mendeleev: The Periodic Table — Convention Guide & Exercises
supplements.description: How Mendeleev organized his periodic table vs. the modern version, periodic trends, and exercises predicting element properties from position

supplements.title: Reading Capital
supplements.description: Recommended selections from Capital Vol. 1 — key chapters on commodities, labor theory of value, surplus value, and primitive accumulation

supplements.title: Reading the Origin of Species
supplements.description: The structure of Darwin's 'one long argument' — how the chapters build on each other, what to watch for, and exercises in applying natural selection reasoning to examples

supplements.title: Riemann and Non-Euclidean Geometry
supplements.description: Framing Riemann's revolution — what does it mean for geometry to be non-Euclidean? The parallel postulate payoff from Euclid, and questions about the geometry of physical space

supplements.title: Bohr Model Exercises
supplements.description: Calculating energy levels, spectral lines, and the hydrogen spectrum using the Bohr model

supplements.title: Curry and Combinatory Logic
supplements.description: Combinatory logic framed for readers coming from Frege and Russell — what combinators are, how they relate to the lambda calculus, and why 'functionality' matters for computation

supplements.title: De Broglie Wave-Particle Exercises
supplements.description: Computing de Broglie wavelengths for various particles and exploring the implications of wave-particle duality

supplements.title: Dirac's Quantum Theory of the Electron
supplements.description: The conceptual core of Dirac's paper — unifying quantum mechanics with special relativity and the prediction of antimatter, framed for readers following the physics conceptually

supplements.title: Einstein: Special Relativity — Notation Guide & Exercises
supplements.description: Einstein's 1905 papers in modern notation — Lorentz transformations, time dilation, length contraction, and the E=mc² derivation with worked exercises

supplements.title: Feynman's Path Integral Approach
supplements.description: Framing the path integral approach to QED — what Feynman diagrams represent, the sum-over-histories idea, and what this paper achieves for quantum field theory

supplements.title: Fisher Statistical Genetics Notation Guide
supplements.description: Fisher's statistical genetics notation translated to modern conventions — the modern synthesis expressed in contemporary terms

supplements.title: Frege and the Logicist Program
supplements.description: The key arguments of Grundlagen der Arithmetik for non-German readers — Frege's logicist program, the definition of number, and why Russell's paradox shattered the foundations

supplements.title: General Relativity — Conceptual Guide
supplements.description: The key ideas of general relativity framed conceptually — equivalence principle, curvature of spacetime, geodesics — without requiring tensor calculus. Pairs the technical 1916 paper with the popular account

supplements.title: Gibbs Statistical Mechanics Notation Guide
supplements.description: Gibbs's statistical mechanics formalism translated to modern notation — ensembles, partition functions, and the bridge from thermodynamics to statistical description

supplements.title: Hilbert's Mathematical Problems
supplements.description: A companion to the 1900 Paris address — context for each problem, which have been solved, which remain open, and how they connect to living mathematics

supplements.title: Lovelace's Notes on the Analytical Engine
supplements.description: Highlighting Note G (the first algorithm), what Lovelace understood about the machine's potential and limitations, and the conceptual leap from calculation to computation

supplements.title: Minkowski Spacetime Notation Guide
supplements.description: The spacetime interval, four-vectors, and Minkowski diagrams — supplementing Minkowski's own exposition with modern notation where needed
